source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn is a crop that removes/uses up a large amount of soil nutrients. To produce good yields, farmers need to know the nutrient needs of this crop. Nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and other minerals must be supplied adequately for growth. If the soil has a pH (KCl) below 5, lime should be applied at a rate of about 500 kg/ha to the plowed field.

Nitrogen (N): nitrogen is the most important nutrient needed for building stems, leaves, roots, flowers, fruit/ear, and for the process of forming amino acids, proteins, vitamins, and enzyme activity. Nitrogen requirement is estimated according to the crop's growth condition; corn needs nitrogen for one growing cycle at a rate of about 190 kg/ha.

Phosphorus (P): phosphorus is also an essential nutrient for corn, important in forming and building new cells; it plays a role in root growth, stem growth, ear formation, tasseling, and flowering/pollination, and in overall corn growth. Total phosphorus requirement for corn is estimated at about 39 kg/ha.

Potassium (K): potassium plays a very important role in forming sugars in fruit crops, in improving grain quality, in disease resistance, and helps with photosynthesis efficiency and water balance within the plant. Corn has been found to take up potassium in especially large amounts, at a stage from about 25 days after planting up to the time it starts flowering and setting fruit.

Total potassium requirement for corn over one growing cycle is estimated at about 196 kg/ha. When there is enough potassium available during growth, it strengthens the plant and improves both fertilizer efficiency and final grain quality.
